characters.name: Martha Vane
characters.status: hale but weary from decades of manual grafting
characters.goal: prove legal authorship of the Wren's Russet pear before the buyout completes

characters.name: Tomas Vane
characters.goal: shield Martha from cooperative liability and prevent the discovery of the scions

characters.name: Julian Gorse
characters.goal: deliver an unencumbered cooperative orchard to AgDev to claim his buyout bonus

characters.name: Judith Callow
characters.goal: ensure her family's cider press shares are honoured in the liquidation

characters.name: Arthur Fenn
characters.goal: preserve the cooperative archive and defend his son Corin's reputation

characters.name: Corin Fenn
characters.goal: complete haulage contracts for AgDev without getting embroiled in valley disputes

characters.name: Beatrice Hale
characters.goal: close the Low Tarn acquisition cleanly on behalf of AgDev Consortium

bag.features: grafting bench, root cellar, stone hearth

objects.name: Notched Copper Grafting Knife
objects.status: honed with a distinct notched heel on the blade bevel

objects.name: 1972 Cooperative Covenant Ledger
objects.status: vellum bound, containing original charter clauses

objects.name: Paraffin-Dipped Scion Crate
objects.status: dormant wood sealed in beeswax and damp moss

premise.logline: An orchard loses a whole variety of pear overnight, and the grafter who bred it has to work out which of her neighbours did it and why.

modules.theme: the difference between owning work and having made it
modules.setting_time: the last autumn before a cooperative is bought out
modules.setting_place: a hill orchard shared by four families who no longer speak
modules.protagonist: a grafter in her sixties who bred the lost variety and never registered it
modules.protagonist_want: to prove the variety was hers before the sale closes
modules.antagonism: a neighbour with a legitimate claim and a bad motive
modules.complication: the person who destroyed the trees did it to protect her
modules.ending_shape: the truth is established and costs the person who established it

plot_shape.name: Mystery
plot_shape.central_question: What actually happened, and who is willing to say so?

phases.name: Disturbance
phases.purpose: A wrong surfaces and someone is obliged to look into it.

phases.name: Inquiry
phases.purpose: Evidence accumulates, most of it true and misread.

phases.name: Wrong turn
phases.purpose: A reading of the evidence that is coherent and wrong collapses.

phases.name: Solution
phases.purpose: The true account, assembled only from what the reader has already been shown.

phases.name: Cost
phases.purpose: What knowing costs the person who found out.

cast_roles.purpose: Carries the reader through the inquiry and pays its cost.
Has a reason to keep the true account from being assembled.
Holds one true piece and misunderstands its meaning.
The reason the question matters at all.

obligatory_moves: Every element of the true account is on the page before it is stated.
At least one true detail is shown early in a context that makes it look irrelevant.
The wrong reading is defensible on the evidence available when it is made.

events.summary: Martha and Tomas discover all fourteen Wren's Russet trees felled and cleanly ring-barked on the high terrace.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: establishes the central crime and reveals the surgical nature of the destruction.
beats: Martha discovers the fourteen mother trees cut to low stumps in the dawn frost.
Martha examines the wounds and observes that the cambium was sliced cleanly rather than torn by a mechanical saw.
Tomas urges her not to report the damage and to let the buyout proceed without trouble.

state_changes.value: shocked and determined to find who destroyed her trees

events.summary: At the packing shed, Beatrice Hale warns Martha that unrecorded varieties will receive no compensation in the sale.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: defines the ticking clock and formal obstacle regarding the unregistered variety.
beats: Martha walks down from the terrace to report the felling to the cooperative committee.
Julian presents AgDev's formal land audit and demands Martha sign the title release.
Beatrice confirms that because Wren's Russet was never formally registered in nursery records, Martha cannot claim ownership or damages.

events.summary: Judith Callow walks the terrace perimeter with Martha, pointing out tyre marks and scuffed blue chalk on the gate.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: plants physical clues at the perimeter while introducing Judith's biased suspicions.
beats: Martha returns to the terrace with Judith to search for signs of vehicle entry.
Judith points out heavy dual-tyre ruts by the top access gate and claims she heard Corin's lorry at midnight.
Martha spots smeared blue timber chalk on the iron latch of the gate.

events.summary: Martha confronts Julian Gorse at his farmhouse, discovering his personal financial stake in an unencumbered sale.
events.dramatic_function: Disturbance: confirms Julian's motive and establishes him as the primary antagonist.
beats: Martha accuses Julian of having her trees cleared to prevent disputes during AgDev's inspection.
Julian retorts that Low Tarn has been broke for five years and cannot afford individual sentimental varieties.
Julian lets slip that AgDev promised him a massive bonus if the orchard transfer closes without outstanding plant patent encumbrances.

events.summary: Martha searches her workshop for her notched copper knife to test stump viability, but discovers it is missing.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: plants a crucial piece of physical evidence in an innocuous domestic scene.
beats: Martha returns to her cottage workshop intending to gather tools to take root samples from the high terrace.
She finds the magnetic tool rack empty of her favourite copper grafting knife.
Tomas claims he misplaced the knife during spring grafting and urges her to leave the dead stumps alone.

events.summary: Martha audits the cooperative tool rack and finds the diesel saw coated in crushed pine, disproving its use on the pears.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: Martha tests a mechanical hypothesis and pays off the initial observation about clean cuts.
beats: Martha inspects the shared cooperative diesel chainsaw in the machinery bay.
Corin admits he borrowed the saw two nights ago on Julian's instructions.
Martha checks the saw's chain teeth and finds gummy softwood sawdust, proving it could not have made the precise cambium cuts on the hardwood pears.

events.summary: Searching the cooperative office desk, Martha finds a draft patent application for Wren's Russet filed under Julian's name.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: discovers apparent documentary proof of Julian's plan to steal her work.
beats: Martha slips into Julian's unlocked cooperative office while the yard is quiet.
She rifles through the buyout correspondence folders inside the metal filing cabinet.
She unearths an AgDev plant breeder patent draft submitted under Julian Gorse's sole name describing the Wren's Russet.

events.summary: Judith Callow insists that Corin and Julian worked together to clear the trees for the patent scheme.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: reinforces the misleading witness testimony with circumstantial conviction.
beats: Martha returns to the terrace to re-examine the felling site alongside Judith.
Judith points to grease marks on the boundary fence and declares she saw Corin's flatbed idling there after dusk.
Judith assures Martha that Julian paid Corin to clear the grove so Julian could claim exclusive patent rights elsewhere.

events.summary: Martha corners Corin Fenn at the Gorse homestead, but Corin refuses to explain his midnight trip.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: intensifies the suspicion around Corin and Julian's secretive nighttime work.
beats: Martha tracks Corin to Julian's gravel yard where he is strapping heavy timber stakes onto his flatbed.
Martha confronts Corin about the tyre ruts and his presence near the high terrace two nights ago.
Julian steps between them, warns Martha against harassing cooperative workers, and orders Corin to stay silent.

events.summary: Arthur Fenn defends his son in the parish hall, producing a delivery log that breaks Corin's alleged link to the pear felling.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: breaks the apparent physical link between Corin's lorry and the severed pear trees.
beats: Martha seeks out Arthur Fenn to demand the truth about Corin's midnight truck run.
Arthur produces AgDev receipt manifests proving Corin was hauling perimeter survey posts to the lower highway boundary all night.
Arthur warns Martha that Corin never climbed the high ridge and tells her she is misreading the orchard's old enmities.

events.summary: Arthur warns Martha that the cooperative's founding charter contains brutal penalties for individual breeding.
events.dramatic_function: Inquiry: surfaces the existence of the cooperative covenant and the legal trap governing orchard stock.
beats: Martha presses Arthur on why everyone is so desperate to silence the question of Wren's Russet.
Arthur reminds her of the 1972 charter signed by the four founding families to stop private commercial side-deals.
Arthur warns Martha that proving private cultivation on cooperative land will ruin whoever did it.

events.summary: Examining the founding ledger in the archive, Martha discovers the severe forfeiture penalty for unauthorized cultivars.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong turn: Martha reads the covenant and constructs a coherent but flawed theory of Julian's extortion.
beats: Martha pulls the vellum cooperative ledger from the parish lockbox.
She finds clause 14 dog-eared, stating that any member breeding unregistered cultivars on co-op rootstock forfeits their land share and cottage.
Martha assumes Julian intends to invoke this clause against her to seize her home along with the pear patent.

events.summary: In the packing shed, Martha publicly accuses Julian of destroying the trees to force her into a covenant forfeiture.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong turn: Martha delivers her accusation based on the patent draft, setting up its collapse.
beats: Martha confronts Julian in front of Beatrice Hale and Tomas, slamming the draft patent onto the sorting table.
She accuses Julian of cutting down the trees to eliminate competition and using the indemnity clause to steal her breeding rights.
Julian reacts with disbelief and counters that he needed the mother trees alive to prove the variety to AgDev.

events.summary: Corin arrives with documented delivery logs and GPS manifests, thoroughly dismantling Martha's case against Julian.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong turn: the false solution collapses completely under verified evidence.
beats: Corin presents signed AgDev delivery manifests confirming he and Julian were at the lower highway junction during the night of the felling.
Beatrice verifies the log stamps and warns Martha that filing unfounded sabotage claims will invalidate her cooperative share.
Martha realizes Julian genuinely needed the living trees to monetize the patent, meaning he had no motive to destroy them.

events.summary: Back at her cottage, Martha tells Tomas she secretly preserved scions in the root cellar, which provokes his panic.
events.dramatic_function: Wrong turn: Martha introduces the living scions, triggering Tomas's emotional unravelling.
beats: Martha retreats to her cottage workshop in defeat, followed by Tomas.
She opens the flagstone hatch to her root cellar and shows him a sealed crate of paraffin-coated scion cuttings taken before the destruction.
Tomas reacts with visible horror rather than relief, begging her to burn the wood and let the variety die.

events.summary: Martha finds blue chalk in Tomas's pocket and her missing copper knife hidden inside his workbench boots.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: the physical clues coalesce to reveal Tomas as the person who cut the trees.
beats: Martha notices blue lumber chalk powder dusting the hem and pockets of Tomas's work coat.
She searches his work crate beneath the grafting table and pulls out her missing notched copper knife wrapped in oiled rag.
Martha confronts Tomas with the knife and the blue chalk, demanding to know why he felled her trees.

events.summary: Tomas confesses that he destroyed the trees to shield Martha from the indemnity clause that would seize her cottage.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: the true protective motive is revealed, completing the causal chain.
beats: Tomas breaks down and admits he used her copper knife to cleanly girdle the trees under cover of dark.
He explains he read the 1972 covenant in the parish ledger weeks ago and overheard Julian planning to report her for illegal private breeding.
He destroyed the trees so there would be no living proof of the variety on co-op land, ensuring Martha could keep her home.

events.summary: Martha decides that establishing that she made the variety is worth losing her home and financial security.
events.dramatic_function: Solution: the protagonist faces the core thematic choice between owning work and having made it.
beats: Tomas begs Martha to cast the scion crate into the hearth fire and let AgDev purchase the land quietly.
Martha refuses to let eighteen years of breeding be erased merely to preserve her financial safety.
She packs the scion crate and the notched knife into her satchel to take them to the final cooperative meeting.

state_changes.value: prove she created Wren's Russet regardless of the legal penalties

events.summary: At the parish hall closing meeting, Martha presents the notched knife and scions to prove she bred the lost pear.
events.dramatic_function: Cost: Martha formally demonstrates the truth to the buyer and the cooperative.
beats: Martha enters the buyout ratification session and places the dormant scions and notched copper knife before Beatrice.
Tomas stands beside her and confirms the knife's chipped heel cut the terrace stumps, matching the wound impressions exactly.
Martha proves Wren's Russet exists, that she bred it over eighteen seasons, and that Julian's patent claim is completely fraudulent.

events.summary: AgDev seizes the scions under the cooperative covenant and forfeits Martha's share, leaving her dispossessed but acknowledged.
events.dramatic_function: Cost: resolution of theme and ending shape; the truth is established at absolute personal expense.
beats: Beatrice accepts the proof of breeding, voids Julian's individual patent claim, and takes legal custody of the scion wood for AgDev.
Invoking clause 14 of the cooperative charter, Beatrice declares Martha's buyout equity and cottage forfeited to AgDev as restitution for unauthorized breeding.
Martha walks out into the cold orchard rain stripped of her land and home, holding only the undeniable knowledge that the pear was hers.

state_changes.value: dispossessed of home and land, but validated as the sole breeder
denied his personal patent and bonus
